# M2-S7: a Go package imports a loGo/s union package (R-U2).
# The Go side sees U as the methods-only interface eject writes: it
# calls functions taking and returning U, holds U in a struct field,
# and type-switches on a result. A Go caller assigning a non-member
# still compiles (a documented hole; loGo/s rejects it, and x.(U)
# checks membership at run time). A union used both as a constraint
# and as a value type fails at the Go import with the pinned text.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

# A Go workspace module imports the loGo/s union package.
cd w
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/union$GOEXE ./g/cmd
exec $WORK/bin/union$GOEXE
stdout '^A:1/A:1/A:1/N/member/non-member$'
cd ..

# loGo/s still rejects a non-member statically.
cd neg
! logos build ./...
stderr 'cannot use .+ as U value'
cd ..

# A dual-use union fails at the Go import.
cd w2
! logos build ./...
stderr 'logos build: union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

-- w/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./l
	./g
)

-- w/l/go.mod --
module example.com/l

go 1.27

-- w/l/u/u.lgo --
package u

import "fmt"

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("A:%d", a.X)
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B:" + b.Y
}

// U is a closed union used as a value type: a parameter, a result,
// and a struct field.
type U interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func Who(x U) string {
	return x.M()
}

func Pick(n int) U {
	if n == 0 {
		return A{X: 1}
	}
	return B{Y: "two"}
}

type Box struct {
	Item U
}

func Check(v any) string {
	if _, ok := v.(U); ok {
		return "member"
	}
	return "non-member"
}

-- w/g/go.mod --
module example.com/g

go 1.27

-- w/g/q/q.go --
package q

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/l/u"
)

// N implements M without being a member of U. Passing it to Who
// compiles on the Go side (a documented hole: loGo/s rejects the
// same assignment) and runs.
type N struct{}

func (n N) M() string { return "N" }

func Describe(x u.U) string {
	switch v := x.(type) {
	case u.A:
		return fmt.Sprintf("A:%d", v.X)
	case u.B:
		return fmt.Sprintf("B:%s", v.Y)
	default:
		return "other"
	}
}

func Run() string {
	a := u.Pick(0)
	out := u.Who(a) + "/" + Describe(a)
	b := u.Box{Item: a}
	out += "/" + u.Who(b.Item)
	out += "/" + u.Who(N{})
	out += "/" + u.Check(u.A{X: 9})
	// 42 implements nothing, so the membership check rejects it on
	// both sides of the boundary.
	out += "/" + u.Check(42)
	return out
}

-- w/g/cmd/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/g/q"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(q.Run())
}

-- neg/go.mod --
module example.com/neg

go 1.27

-- neg/neg.lgo --
package neg

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

// C implements M but is not a member of U.
type C struct {
	Z int
}

func (c C) M() string {
	return "C"
}

type U interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

var _ U = C{Z: 1}

-- w2/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./l2
	./g2
)

-- w2/l2/go.mod --
module example.com/l2

go 1.27

-- w2/l2/d/d.lgo --
package d

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

// D is used as a constraint and as a value: it has no Go form, so the
// package builds but a Go package that imports it fails.
type D interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func First[T D](x T) T {
	return x
}

var V D = A{X: 1}

func Msg() string {
	return First(B{Y: "q"}).M() + V.M()
}

-- w2/g2/go.mod --
module example.com/g2

go 1.27

-- w2/g2/q/q.go --
package q

import "example.com/l2/d"

func Run() string {
	return d.Msg()
}

-- w2/g2/cmd/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/g2/q"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(q.Run())
}
